issue.title: Codex usage probe leaks sase-codex-usage-* tempdirs outside the managed tmp root, tripping the tmp-leak guard
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-14y.2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #6, 2026-09-21) and routed by the sase-14y land agent.

`collect_codex_usage` in `src/sase/llm_provider/usage/codex_collector.py:72` creates its
app-server cwd with a raw `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="sase-codex-usage-")`, bypassing
`sase.core.paths.get_sase_managed_tmpdir`. When a codex usage probe is still running (or its
cleanup has not run) at test teardown, the `sase-codex-usage-*` dir lands in the system temp
root and the tmp-leak guard (`tests/_tmp_leak_guard.py`) fails intermittently. During the
sase-14y.2 golden refresh this blocked `just fix-tui-screenshots` until goldens were banked with
`SASE_TMP_LEAK_GUARD_DISABLED=1`.

Fix: create the cwd under `get_sase_managed_tmpdir(...)` (and make cleanup robust on every exit
path), then add a regression test.

task_type_fields.impact: Intermittently fails the tmp-leak guard and blocks golden banking; forces SASE_TMP_LEAK_GUARD_DISABLED workarounds.
task_type_fields.repro: Run the visual lane / fix-tui-screenshots on a host with the codex CLI; the tmp-leak guard intermittently reports sase-codex-usage-* dirs left in the system temp root (observed by sase-14y.2 on 2026-09-21).
